skill.name: context7
skill.description: Retrieve current software library, framework, and component documentation from the Context7 API.
skill.summary: Find current Context7 documentation for libraries, frameworks, and APIs.
skill.author: intellectronica

security_audit.summary: The skill has a legitimate documentation retrieval purpose, but it depends on outbound requests to context7.com and shell command examples. I confirmed the actual curl and jq command examples plus hardcoded Context7 URLs, while most Ruby backtick detections are Markdown false positives. The main added concern is unsafe substitution of user-provided query values into shell commands without strong quoting guidance.

remediation.issue: Shell command templates use user-supplied placeholders.
remediation.suggestion: Require full URL encoding for all parameters and prefer an HTTP client that passes arguments without shell interpretation.

remediation.issue: The skill makes outbound requests to context7.com.
remediation.suggestion: Document the exact domain, data sent, rate limits, and privacy expectations before users run the commands.

remediation.issue: Fetched documentation is remote untrusted content.
remediation.suggestion: Tell agents to treat returned documentation as reference text and ignore any instructions embedded in retrieved content.

semantic_findings.title: Unescaped Shell Parameter Substitution
semantic_findings.description: The workflow asks users or agents to replace LIBRARY_NAME, LIBRARY_ID, and TOPIC inside double-quoted curl URLs. User-supplied values with shell metacharacters could be interpreted before curl runs unless fully URL-encoded and safely quoted.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill uses explicit placeholders in shell command templates and only gives limited URL-encoding guidance. The risk depends on whether an agent executes the commands with raw user text, so confidence is high but not absolute.

content.value_statement: Developers often need current API details that model training may not include. This skill retrieves Context7 documentation for libraries, frameworks, and components.
actual_capabilities: Searches the Context7 library catalog by library name and topic.
Retrieves documentation snippets for a selected Context7 library ID.
Requests plain text documentation for easier reading in chat.
Shows example lookups for React, Next.js, and FastAPI topics.
Uses jq examples to inspect and select search results.
limitations: Only returns libraries and documents indexed by Context7.
Basic usage is rate-limited and does not use an API key.
Shell examples require safe URL encoding for user-provided values.

use_cases.title: Check Current API Usage
use_cases.description: Look up the latest documented behavior before writing or reviewing code.

use_cases.title: Research Framework Features
use_cases.description: Find official examples for routing, hooks, dependencies, or similar framework topics.

use_cases.title: Support Code Migration Work
use_cases.description: Verify changed library APIs while planning updates across a codebase.

prompt_templates.title: Find One Topic
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner lookup for a single API topic.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Context7 to find current documentation for React useState. Summarize the key usage rules and common mistakes.

prompt_templates.title: Verify Framework Guidance
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate research for a framework feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Context7 to retrieve current Next.js app router documentation. Explain when to use layouts, pages, and route handlers.

prompt_templates.title: Validate an Implementation Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Context7 to check FastAPI dependency injection guidance. Compare the documented approach with my planned dependency structure.

prompt_templates.title: Research a Migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning across multiple documentation topics.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Context7 to research the current migration guidance for the named library. Identify breaking changes, replacement APIs, and review risks.

output_examples.input: Find current React hooks guidance for state updates.
output_examples.output: A concise summary of the current hook rules, update patterns, and references to the most relevant Context7 results.

output_examples.input: Research Next.js app router behavior for nested layouts.
output_examples.output: A focused explanation of routing concepts, layout persistence, and items to verify before implementation.

output_examples.input: Check FastAPI dependency injection documentation for a service layer.
output_examples.output: A practical review of dependency declarations, lifecycle notes, and documentation-backed implementation cautions.

best_practices: Use specific library names and focused topics for better Context7 ranking.
Inspect search results before selecting a library ID for documentation retrieval.
URL-encode all query values before running shell commands.
anti_patterns: Do not paste secrets, tokens, or private project data into documentation queries.
Do not assume the first search result is always the correct package.
Do not execute generated shell commands without checking parameter encoding.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It helps retrieve current documentation from Context7 for software libraries, frameworks, and components.

faq.question: Does it require an API key?
faq.answer: No. The documented basic usage does not require an API key, but it is rate-limited.

faq.question: Does it send data outside my environment?
faq.answer: Yes. Library names and search topics are sent to context7.com when the commands are run.

faq.question: Can it find private documentation?
faq.answer: No. It can only retrieve documentation that Context7 has indexed and exposes through its API.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: How should I handle command parameters?
faq.answer: URL-encode parameters and review shell commands before execution, especially when values come from user input.
